297.t: Gaspard's age and death after Summers' father
297.s: Gaspard died at about 86 shortly after Summers' father; the family had moved to New Orleans in 1910.
297.q: Good English. He's a man about, well, he oughta been about 80 or something too now. I guess he would, oh yeah. About 86, you know.

621.s: Russell and Duhé recall Mutt Carey, who died in 1948, and talk about his Hahnville origins and a recent parade there.
621.q: I knew Mutt very well. Wonderful trumpet playing. His style of playing.

713.s: Nelson says his brother played in bands mostly in Raceland, died about twenty years ago, and was known as Stanks.
713.ch: Second reel: instrument, style and wrap-up
713.q: Yeah, he played in some bands up here. But he mostly was in Raceland. He didn't have bands? I don't know what band he'd be in up there, you see.

665.s: Brother Philip Grace died around 1954 and did not play music.
665.q: He's been dead. Since... Let's see. 50... 50... 54... He died. That's...

293.t: Peter Alexander and his son P.J.
293.s: Peter Alexander is dead and has a son in Baltimore called P.J.
293.ch: Violinists, Jimmy Noon and Decatur Street
293.q: Yeah, he died. He's got a son who lives in Baltimore, Maryland. What's his son's name? Well, we call him P.J. Alexander. Now what that P.J. stands for, I don't know. Well, it could be Peter Junior.

760.t: The death of John Robichaux while Joe was on tour
760.s: His uncle's final illness, Joe's booking trip through Florida and the Gulf, and his uncle's death and burial before he returned.
760.q: Yeah, well I appreciate it. And so anyway, after they disbanded the theater, my uncle he played around a while, but he got sick and he disbanded the band.

109.t: His brother takes up drums and has just died
109.s: His brother became a good drummer after Kenny did; he died two months before the interview.
109.q: Then he wanted to play the drums too. He was a very good drummer, a very good drummer.

88.t: His father's death and the end of the band
88.s: Lee's father died around 1942 or 1943, and the band was not kept together after he came home from New York.
88.ch: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
88.q: No. They didn't keep it. They disbande. Yeah, I had to be with it because nobody was gonna take care of the business, and I was kind of business oriented, and I took care of it, but that was really the end of the band. We didn't ever fool with it again.

90.t: The club closes and the band breaks up
90.s: The owner Mister Jones died and his niece closed the club; his grandmother fell ill and died.
90.ch: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
90.q: So we kept on. I worked there and worked there and worked there. And Mister Jones passed, who owned the club, and his niece was trying to run the place, and she couldn't really handle it, so she decided to give it up. So the band disbanded, and the place was shut down. And it wasn't too

18.t: Eutris on his place in history
18.s: She thinks he was among the greatest trombonists and is hurt that he can no longer play.
18.ch: Favorite bands, advice and family reflections
18.q: I don't think he has accomplished as much as he was able to do because I thought he was one of the greatest trombone players in the whole world. I have never in my life heard anyone play like him. And I was so hurt and I'm still hurt that he's not able to play the trombone like he used to. Never…
